title: Metric contract
description: One definition, four consumers: a dbt model, a SQL table function, the agent's tool definition and the experiment readout query. The contract compiles into all four; none of them may hold a second definition.

supersedes.description: The version this one replaces, or null for the first. No metric version is ever deleted.

grain.description: The columns the metric is defined per. Every source must expose all of them.

expression.description: A signed sum of sum(...) aggregate terms, each referencing exactly one declared source alias: <expression> ::= <term> { ("+"|"-") <term> }, <term> ::= "sum" "(" <inner> ")". The grammar is enforced by the compiler, not only described here. A term straddling two relations could not be aggregated to the grain without fanning out, so it is refused rather than guessed at. The expression is rendered from one parse into every consumer; no consumer rewrites it.

sources.description: The relations the expression reads, each bound to the alias the expression uses. The first source is the anchor; every other declares how it joins to it. Without this binding the expression could not be compiled and each consumer would have to guess the join — which is exactly the second definition the contract exists to prevent.

why_the_readout_needs_it.description: Every metric earns its place or it is padding. One sentence naming the failure it makes visible.

restatement.description: Doctrine rule 4 — a change that affects past values restates rather than overwrites. Present on any version whose definition changed the meaning of an earlier number.

provenance.description: Where the definition comes from. Required, because the metric family was the only one in this repository with nowhere to say 'this is the scenario speaking', and a file that reads as history when it is a fixture is exactly the kind of thing nobody notices twice.
